claims.sentence: The MHRA has approved icotrokinra (Icotyde), a once-daily tablet, for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in people aged 12 and over.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: authorisation for icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) granted 23 October 2026 to Janssen-Cilag Limited; moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12+ weighing at least 40 kg who are candidates for systemic therapy; 200mg tablet once a day; four Phase 3 trials, 2,500 people, incl. 72 adolescents aged 12 to under 18 weighing at least 40 kg. (Weight >=40 kg qualifier is omitted in the summary; acceptable shorthand but body states it.)

claims.sentence: The MHRA approved icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in October 2026.
The approval covers adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: authorisation for icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) granted 23 October 2026 to Janssen-Cilag Limited; moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12+ weighing at least 40 kg who are candidates for systemic therapy; 200mg tablet once a day; four Phase 3 trials, 2,500 people, incl. 72 adolescents aged 12 to under 18 weighing at least 40 kg.

claims.sentence: It applies to people who are candidates for systemic therapy.
The MHRA says four phase 3 trials with about 2,500 participants showed benefit over placebo at week 16.
claims.evidence: Four Phase 3 trials with 2,500 people confirmed, but neither retrieval mentions placebo comparison, 'benefit' or week 16.
claims.newSentence: The MHRA says its approval was supported by data from four phase 3 trials with about 2,500 participants.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says it has approved icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: authorisation for icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) granted 23 October 2026 to Janssen-Cilag Limited; moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12+ weighing at least 40 kg who are candidates for systemic therapy; 200mg tablet once a day; four Phase 3 trials, 2,500 people, incl. 72 adolescents aged 12 to under 18 weighing at least 40 kg.

claims.sentence: The medicine is a tablet taken once a day, and the marketing authorisation was granted to Janssen-Cilag Limited.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: taken as a 200mg tablet once a day; authorisation granted to Janssen-Cilag Limited. (Dose deliberately not stated in brief.)

claims.sentence: The approval applies to people who are candidates for systemic therapy, which means treatment that acts throughout the body rather than on the skin alone.
claims.evidence: First half retrieved. The definition of 'systemic therapy' is a gloss not in the retrieved text; it is a plain-language definition and accurate, but strictly it is the author's explanation, not the source's.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says its decision rested on four phase 3 trials with about 2,500 participants, 72 of them adolescents aged 12 to under 18 who weighed at least 40 kg.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: approval supported by four Phase 3 trials, 2,500 people, including 72 adolescents aged 12 to under 18 weighing at least 40 kg. ('rested on' vs 'supported by' is a minor shift.)
claims.newSentence: The MHRA says its approval was supported by four phase 3 trials with about 2,500 participants, 72 of them adolescents aged 12 to under 18 who weighed at least 40 kg.

claims.sentence: In all four trials, icotrokinra showed benefit over placebo at week 16.
claims.evidence: No retrieved text mentions placebo, week 16 or per-trial outcomes.

claims.sentence: The site's psoriasis page explains the condition.
claims.evidence: Site-navigation pointer to another page on this site, not a claim from the MHRA page; the retrieved gov.uk text does not mention it.

dateEvidence: Search 1 and 2 both returned: authorisation granted 23 October 2026. The news story's own 'Published' date was not returned; search 2 said the page metadata shows it posted 11 days before 3 November (= 23 October), an inference. First-pass note of a 21 Oct listing was not corroborated.
notes: Brief's published 2026-10-23 is probably right (matches authorisation date and the '11 days' age) but the page's printed date was not read, so dateConfirmed is null. Retrieval also said the MHRA will monitor safety and asks for Yellow Card reports and that the SmPC/leaflets go to MHRA Products within 7 days of approval; none is used in the brief. No instructions, 'safe' claims or doses in the brief. Does not warrant dropping the brief.
